goal: Evaluate the delivered model on a second cohort. Open item 1 in the README and PROJECT_REPORT, and per section 6e the only remaining move that buys statistical power and clinical credibility at once.
status: BLOCKED on data, not on effort.

data/mesa/features/*.csv.content: DERIVED night-level sleep architecture - TST_sec, Sleep_Efficiency, SOL_sec, WASO_sec, per-stage durations and proportions
data/mesa/features/*.csv.why: This is the OUTPUT of physiological_features.extract_features, computed from someone else's scoring. It is the same kind of object the evidence packet produces, not the signal a stager consumes. There is no EEG here.

cfs_preprocessed/*.pt.content: SEVEN channels x 3000 samples = ONE 30-second epoch per subject
cfs_preprocessed/*.pt.why: One epoch is not a night. Staging needs the full recording - the model reads 256-epoch windows and every derived metric (sleep efficiency, REM latency, WASO) is defined over a whole night. 82 KB per subject against the ~40 MB a night of 3-channel signal occupies confirms it: this is a sample, probably a preprocessing smoke test.

what_is_missing: The raw PSG recordings. NSRR distributes CFS and MESA polysomnography as EDF, gated behind a data-use agreement; a request appears to have been filed (sleepdata.org_data_requests_27860). Nothing in this repository can substitute for it.
additional_work_once_the_signal_exists: Channel mapping. CFS and MESA use different montages and sampling rates from Sleep-EDFx. The model expects Fpz-Cz at 100 Hz; NSRR cohorts typically provide C3/C4-referenced derivations at 128 or 256 Hz. Resampling and re-referencing is a design decision, not a conversion, and it is the sort of decision that quietly invalidates a comparison if made silently.
The 34 spectral features must be recomputed by the same code path, or the spectral stream receives something it was never trained on.
Annotation vocabulary. NSRR XML uses its own stage names; the W/N1/N2/N3/REM mapping must be explicit and asserted, exactly as STAGE_MAP is in preprocess_multichannel.py.

preprocess_multichannel.py --verify has no counterpart here: there are no existing tensors to reproduce. A different integrity check is needed - most likely comparing derived sleep architecture against the cohort's own published summaries, which for MESA are the feature CSVs already on disk.
honest_expectation: Kappa will fall. CFS and MESA are clinical populations with sleep pathology, recorded on different hardware, against Sleep-EDFx's largely healthy adults. A drop measured properly is a stronger result than another tie on Sleep-EDFx, and the size of the drop is the finding.
recommendation: Do not improvise around the missing data. Staging a single epoch, or scoring against MESA's derived features without predictions to compare them to, would produce a number with nothing behind it.
